branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Sentinel Home narrows, delays, or rolls back the increase for legacy customers.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Public retention offer, grandfathering announcement, or revised pricing notice appears before formal regulatory action.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Early churn, cancellations, or support distress exceed management tolerance.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Most legacy customers absorb the increase with modest concessions and limited net churn.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Complaint volume remains high while actual cancellation and migration evidence stays comparatively low over multiple ticks.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Customer anger stays expressive but switching remains cumbersome and scattered.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Regulators pressure a settlement involving disclosures, transition rights, or pricing concessions rather than immediate hard sanction.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Formal information requests, settlement language, or company commitments on migration fairness become visible.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Evidence accumulates that lock-in or exit barriers materially weaken customer choice.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Rivals capture a meaningful share of dissatisfied users, weakening incumbent pricing leverage.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Publicized migration numbers, repeated customer testimonials, or expanded rival acquisition spend appears.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Migration discounts combine with visible success stories that reduce perceived switching risk.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Conflict cools enough to avoid major churn and formal sanction while headline increase partly survives.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Mixed customer response with reduced anger and no full reversal, alongside messaging about fairness adjustments.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Company offers selective credits, phased implementation, or legacy plan modifications that soften backlash.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Selective credits or partial delays alone do not realize this endpoint unless they substantially neutralize the increase for most legacy users.
endpoint_ledger.description: The company fully reverses or materially withdraws the announced increase for the affected legacy base.
endpoint_ledger.label: Legacy price increase rolled back

meta.important_question: Will Sentinel Home fully or substantially roll back the legacy subscription price increase?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Management has direct authority, but will likely require strong churn or scrutiny signals.
realization_criteria: Official company announcement rescinds or substantially reverses the increase for most legacy customers.
Billing or plan notices show legacy customers broadly remain on prior pricing or equivalent effective pricing.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Rollback is explicitly named as a plausible endpoint but not chosen at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: High complaint volume without elevated actual cancellations does not realize this endpoint.
endpoint_ledger.description: A meaningful share of legacy customers cancels or migrates, reducing the company's retention position.
endpoint_ledger.label: Material churn wave

meta.important_question: Will legacy-customer dissatisfaction convert into materially elevated churn rather than mostly expressive backlash?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Distributed customer decisions determine this outcome; rivals can accelerate it by lowering friction.
realization_criteria: Reported or credibly observed cancellations/migrations exceed normal attrition by a clearly material margin.
Competitors or the company acknowledge sustained elevated switching from legacy plans.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Customers threaten cancellation at T0, but behavioral conversion remains unresolved.

blockers: limited evidence of unlawful or unfair lock-in
company voluntary concessions that reduce appetite for formal action
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Informal inquiries or press statements alone do not realize this endpoint absent a visible corrective arrangement.
endpoint_ledger.description: Regulatory scrutiny results in a visible settlement, consent commitment, or equivalent corrective arrangement regarding lock-in or transition fairness.
endpoint_ledger.label: Regulatory settlement or corrective commitment

meta.important_question: Will regulator concern over lock-in mature into a visible settlement or enforceable corrective commitment?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Regulators have conditional authority, but need evidence and process to move from questions to settlement.
realization_criteria: Regulators announce a settlement, binding commitment, or formal corrective agreement with Sentinel Home.
Company adopts regulator-linked remedies such as migration rights, disclosures, or constrained repricing under official resolution.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly includes regulators asking about lock-in, but no formal action exists yet.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A narrow temporary pause or isolated retention offer does not negate this endpoint if the broader increase still holds.
endpoint_ledger.description: The company retains the core increase and most legacy customers remain despite backlash, perhaps with minor concessions.
endpoint_ledger.label: Price increase broadly sticks

meta.important_question: Will the company retain the core price increase with only limited concessions and broad customer acceptance/inertia?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint depends on company resolve interacting with customer inertia and weak enforcement pressure.
realization_criteria: Core higher pricing remains in force for most legacy customers after the controversy window.
Observed churn and regulatory action remain limited enough that the company does not materially reverse course.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Accepted price increase is named as a plausible endpoint and supported by customer inertia and switching costs.

merge_hypotheses.convergence_driver: Shared reluctance to disrupt home-security service can pull angry and quiet customers back toward staying behavior unless migration becomes clearly safe.
Regulators may prefer incremental inquiry and settlement, causing divergent public narratives to converge on a moderate compliance path.
Even limited concessions can satisfy enough inertial customers to reduce mobilization and compress branch differences.

risk_flags.note: Installed base, revenue exposure, and market concentration are unspecified, limiting precise churn and regulatory weight calibration.
Scenario references lock-in but does not specify whether barriers are contractual, technical, hardware-bound, or data portability related.
Type and strength of regulator authority are not identified at T0.
Endpoint competition depends heavily on migration friction and ownership leverage, but these are only qualitatively implied.
Complaint visibility may overstate broader customer willingness to churn due to silent inertial segments.

simulation_brief.summary: A fictional home-security company raises subscription prices for legacy customers, triggering customer cancellation threats, competitive migration offers, and regulatory scrutiny over lock-in. The company cites cloud cost pressure. T0 should emphasize switching costs, platform ownership leverage, trust, and unresolved endpoint competition between rollback, churn, regulatory settlement, or customer acceptance of the increase.
simulation_brief.time_zero_posture: early controversy with unresolved commercial and regulatory pressure, not yet at terminal outcome
uncertainty_notes: No company size, geography, installed base, or exact price delta specified.
Regulatory authority and formal legal posture are not specified at T0.
Competitor identities and customer segmentation are inferred generically from scenario framing.

sociology_baseline.note: Customers may update views through peers and coverage, but loyalists and inertial users will not immediately converge with angrier segments.
Visible successful switching or concessions could tip quiet dissatisfaction into broader action.
Many dissatisfied users remain quiet because of hassle, uncertainty, or security continuity dependence.
Legacy customers are likely to trust similar users' migration stories more than corporate messaging.
Repeated reports of painless migration are more likely than a single complaint to trigger wider switching.
Some customers identify with brand reliability, slowing uniform backlash.
Without new revelations, issue salience may fade even if practical customer anger remains.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Observed ease or difficulty of moving to rival systems will shape whether complaint stays expressive or becomes behavioral.
Whether public discourse frames the increase as routine repricing or exploitative lock-in will influence legitimacy.
Competitor discount visibility can convert passive dissatisfaction into comparison shopping.
Fear of losing home-security reliability suppresses public action and churn among inertial customers.
A mild inquiry versus formal scrutiny changes perceptions of company vulnerability and fairness.
